entries.title: Bears' defense — the No-Names of the Midway? — is standing up and demanding to be noticed
entries.summary: <p>The No-Names of the Midway held the Jets’ offense to 157 yards Sunday in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/04/bears-jets-qb-tyson-bagent-13-3-halftime-score-uneven-soldier-field-cairo-santos-case-keenum-nfl" target="_blank" >a 23-12 win at Soldier Field</a>. And all of seven first downs. And zero third-down conversions. And pretty much no hope, dignity or semblance of NFL-caliber ability.</p><p>If it weren’t for one fourth-quarter bomb from Jets quarterback Geno Smith to former Illinois star Isaiah Williams, the game would have been absurdly one-sided. Then again, it was anyway.</p><p>Sure, we could throw a parade for the Bears’ offense, which had a big day and possessed the football for more than two-thirds of the game. We could compose odes to coach Ben Johnson’s offensive brilliance after the team’s third win of the season with a different quarterback. We could talk about injured starter Caleb Williams, too, because when is talking about Williams ever a bad idea?</p><p>Williams and Johnson are the objects of our obsession, let’s face it. That goes for the fans and the local media, too.</p><p>But the defense? You know, the part of the team nobody ever really talks about? The No-Names had a little something to do with how this one went down, you know.</p><p>After holding the Vikings and Eagles to a combined 16 points the last two weeks, the Bears nearly made it three straight games allowing single-digit points — which would’ve been a first for them since 1988.</p><p>“It’s incredible to see guys just go out there and ball,” rookie safety Dillon Thieneman said.</p><p>There were three Jets three-and-outs. Twice after Bears turnovers in their own territory, the defense shrugged off the tension of the moment, held the Jets to field goals and squashed any momentum for the visitors.</p><p>Yes, it helps to face a Vikings team quarterbacked by Carson Wentz and a Jets team that is, ahem, the Jets. Putting a good defensive stretch together under those circumstances might not mean the rest of the offenses on the Bears schedule — starting with the Packers next weekend — should be quaking in their cleats.</p><p>But it’s starting to look like a well-balanced Bears team, obsessions aside.</p><p>“It feels good, but the job’s not done,” said end Dayo Odeyingbo, who was credited with one sack and helped set up another with a lightning-quick rush that forced Smith to step up in the pocket right into a charging Austin Booker. “This league is like, ‘What have you done for me lately?’ ”</p><p>Lately, the No-Names are more than holding their own.</p><p>It’s nice when your offense has the ball for 42-plus minutes. That’s not merely the offense’s doing, though.</p><p>“Probably one of the easiest NFL games I’ve played in,” linebacker Devin Bush said. “I’m not sore at all, so it was great.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Dayo being disruptive 👀<br><br>Austin Booker with a perfectly timed jump to get in Geno Smith’s passing lane to come away with the sack. <br><br>Bears defense. 📈 <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/DaBears?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#DaBears</a> <a href="https://t.co/TmcAKKOSdX">pic.twitter.com/TmcAKKOSdX</a></p>— Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) <a href="https://x.com/clayharbs82/status/2106804523692064802?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 4, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3></h3><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><h3><b>TRANSLATION STATION</b></h3><p><b>What Booker said: </b>“Obviously, you want to be on the field more.”</p><p><b>What he meant: </b>“Did you see who we were playing?”</p><p><b>What defensive tackle Grady Jarrett said: </b>“We’ve got a lot of respect for [the Jets]. … I think they’ve got a really good team.”</p><p><b>What he meant: </b>“But seriously, folks.”</p><p><b>What Johnson said in the locker room: </b>“You guys know what next week is? entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Packers beat Buccaneers 17-14 behind Jordan Love's 2 touchdown passes
entries.summary: <p>TAMPA, Fla. — An ugly win left the Green Bay Packers dissatisfied.</p><p>Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes and the Packers overcame two fourth-quarter turnovers to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 17-14 on Sunday.</p><p>Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels threw two picks that led to 10 points in his first career start filling in for Baker Mayfield, who missed a game for the first time in his three-plus seasons in Tampa Bay because of a dislocated thumb.</p><p>The Packers (2-2) wasted two opportunities to extend a three-point lead in the fourth quarter but the Buccaneers couldn't capitalize.</p><p>"There were some positive things but we're never going to be satisfied with scoring 17 points in a game," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. "That's just not to our standard and we have to find ways when we're in the red area to convert. We can't be turning the ball over. We can't have penalties. That is a stingy defense. You have to give them a lot of credit. … But we also have to clean up a lot of stuff. It's gotta get fixed and it's gotta get fixed now."</p><p>Tykee Smith forced Kaleb Johnson to fumble inside the 5 with just over nine minutes left in the game. A'Shawn Robinson recovered at the 4 but the ensuing drive went nowhere.</p><p>"A great teacher is the bench. If guys don't start holding onto the ball, they're gonna be sitting on the bench," LaFleur said bluntly.</p><p>The Packers then had a first-and-15 at the Buccaneers 26 when Jacob Parrish picked Love's pass and gave Tampa Bay the ball at the 15 and a chance for a comeback win.</p><p>Instead, Daniels threw a short screen pass to Emeka Egbuka on third-and-16 and incomplete on fourth down from the Packers 47. Coach Todd Bowles passed up a 65-yard field-goal attempt by Chase McLaughlin, who made one from that distance last year.</p><p>Bowles said a little wind factored into the decision not to try it.</p><p>The Buccaneers are 0-4 for the first time since 2014. Only the 1992 Chargers overcame an 0-4 start to make the playoffs.</p><p>"I'm the head coach. I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame," Bowles said. "We're gonna fight, we're gonna stick together and we're gonna figure this thing out. And I'll lead them to that. It's my job."</p><p>Love tossed a 2-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden on fourth down to give the Packers a 7-0 lead in the second quarter. Evan Williams made a sliding interception near the sideline to give Green Bay the ball at the 32. Love connected with Tucker Kraft for 10 yards on fourth-and-1 to keep the drive going. Kraft also took a direct snap and sneaked for a first down on another fourth-and-1 at the Buccaneers 10.</p><p>The Packers turned an interception by Edgerrin Cooper in the final minute of the first half into a field goal. Cooper stepped in front of Daniels' pass to Kameron Johnson, caught the ball falling to the ground, got up and returned it 18 yards to the Buccaneers 44. Trey Smack kicked a 58-yarder to give Green Bay a 10-7 lead.</p><p>Love's 2-yard TD pass to Kraft on the opening drive of the third quarter extended the lead to 17-7.</p><p>"We'll take the win for sure. It was sloppy on those last drives," Love said. "We have a chance to put the game out of reach. Two turnovers is unacceptable. That's something we have to clean up. … That was the disappointing part of the game."</p><p>Sean Tucker ran in from the 2 to tie it at 7. Daniels completed both of his passes for 27 yards combined on the drive and scrambled 9 yards before Tucker's score.</p><p>Daniels connected with Kenneth Gainwell on a 10-yard TD pass to cut the deficit to 17-14 early in the fourth quarter.</p><h3>Depleted Packers</h3><h3></h3><p>Cooper was carted off the field in the third quarter with an Achilles tendon injury. The Packers are still missing three-time All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons, who is recovering from surgery for a torn ACL suffered last December.</p><p>Love got his best protection this season despite playing played behind an offensive line missing three starters: Zach Bako-Bewele, Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk. Laken Tomlinson became the fourth player to start at left guard. Veteran guard Kevin Zeitler signed earlier in the week was inactive.</p><p>After taking 31 QB hits in the first three games, Love took two.</p><p>"The O-line did a great job," Love said. "Pass protection, run game, just keeping me clean and giving me time. They did a great job and you can feel the difference back there for sure."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><p><b>Packers:</b> CB Brandon Cisse hurt his neck and was being evaluated for concussion. ... LB Isaiah McDuffie replaced Cooper and briefly left with an eye injury. ... RB Chris Brooks and DT Devonte Wyatt both left in the first half with ankle injuries. ... Banks (toe, knee) and Monk (quadriceps) will return while Bako-Bewele (knee) is out for the season.</p><p><b>Buccaneers:</b> Edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. (groin), CB Benjamin Morrison (quadriceps), TE Ko Kieft (elbow) were inactive. ... S Antoine Winfield Jr. hurt his abdomen and a rib late in the fourth quarter. ... LB SirVocea Dennis injured his ankle.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Packers:</b> Host the Bears next Sunday.</p><p><b>Buccaneers:</b> Visit Dallas on Thursday night.<br></p>
